extension.description: A configurable video add-on for Kodi. Browse categories, search, keep favorites and a resume-aware watch history, and play from a content source you configure. Content-source agnostic: point it at your own JSON API or HTML source.
extension.news: v1.2.0 - Continue Watching: a root-menu row (and ?action=widget&type=continue for skins) listing anything you started but did not finish, backed by the existing watch history + resume points. Auto-play next: an opt-in setting (off by default) that, when a video in a category listing finishes, automatically plays the next item in that category (or the next page's first item). Sort and filter: category listings gained a "Sort by..." entry (title / rating / release date / duration) plus native Kodi duration sorting, and a "Minimum rating" setting that hides videos below a threshold across categories, search and widgets. v1.1.6 - Fixed the Settings -> Base API URL field, which was silently disconnected from every request (any source you typed there was ignored; only a source added via the multi-source manager ever worked). Fixed the Switch source menu item crashing on every use. Added a "static (no server)" content source mode, so a Kodi repository alone (GitHub Pages, any plain file host -- no code to run, no computer to keep on) can serve a working demo catalogue; see tools/build_static_demo.py. v1.1.5 - Five features added: resume badges with progress percentage in video listings (Progress, ResumeLabel properties); Trakt.tv scrobbling to track watch progress across devices (trakt_id on videos, trakt_enabled/username/token settings); subtitle URL passing on streams (subtitle field on Stream, setSubtitles); watch progress percentage in listings; and a content source switcher (multiple sources in sources.json, Switch source action). v1.1.4 - Preview images: videos may now include an optional "preview" URL (a still or animated frame). When provided it is shown as the listing's fanart/background image so the video content is identifiable at a glance; "thumb" remains the poster thumbnail.
